app.name: TxRecover
app.tagline: Neighbors with winches, not a tow bill.

home.emergencyNote: If anyone is hurt, in water, or in traffic, call 911 first. We are volunteers, not emergency services.
home.how1: Tell us where you are and how you're stuck. Takes about two minutes.
home.how2: We text the nearest volunteers with the right gear. The first one to answer takes it.
home.how3: You get their name and an ETA, and a link you can watch until you're out.
home.volunteerSoon: Volunteer signup opens soon. If you already pull people out in the Facebook groups, this is for you.

legal.privacyBody:
PLACEHOLDER — REVIEW WITH LAWYER.

What we collect

- Your name and mobile number, so a volunteer can reach you.
- The location you give us, and how accurate it was.
- Any photos you upload. These are shrunk and stripped of camera metadata on your phone before they reach us.
- Your IP address and browser user agent at the moment you accept the waiver, because that acceptance is a legal record.

Who sees what

- Your phone number is never shown publicly. It is released to one person: the volunteer who accepts your request.
- Your exact location is never shown publicly. The public board shows a pin moved about a mile off.
- Volunteers who were notified but did not take the job never see your name, number or exact location.
- Administrators can see everything, because somebody has to be able to sort out a job that goes wrong.

How long we keep it

- REVIEW WITH LAWYER: set a retention period here.

Who we share it with

- Twilio, to send the text messages.
- Supabase, which hosts the database and the photos.
- Mapbox, which draws the map. Mapbox receives map tile requests from your browser.
- Nobody else. We do not sell anything, and we do not hand lists of stranded drivers to towing companies.

>>> REVIEW WITH LAWYER <<<
